Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagbubuhos ng likido?

Pwede mong ibuhos at haluin ang likido tulad ng tubig! Humihiwalay ito kapag binuhos, at muling nagsasama sa lalagyan.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung magbubo og likido?

Mahimo nimong ibubo ug kutawon ang likido sama sa tubig! Mabahin kini kung ibubo, ug magtipon balik sa sudlanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are 1,000 milliliters in one whole liter.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the conversion factor between milliliters and liters but does not involve using measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume, which is the core action of the competency. It provides background knowledge for measuring with these units.

copy.en:
How many milliliters of water fill up one liter?

Great job! There are 1,000 milliliters in one whole liter. That is a lot of liquid!
copy.tl:
Ilang mililitro ng tubig ang nagpupuno sa isang litro?

Magaling! May 1,000 mililitro sa isang buong litro. Iyon ay napakaraming likido!
copy.bis:
Pila ka mililitro nga tubig ang nagpuno sa usa ka litro?

Maayo! Adunay 1,000 ka mililitro sa usa ka tibuok litro. Daghan kaayo na nga likido!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one whole liter is exactly equal to 1,000 milliliters
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the conversion between liters and milliliters. It does not teach how to use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume, which is the core action of the competency. The conversion is useful background knowledge for measuring volume but does not directly support the skill.

copy.en: Did you know that one whole liter is exactly equal to 1,000 milliliters? That is a lot!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na isang buong litro ay katumbas ng 1,000 mililitro? Nakakamangha, 'di ba!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga usa ka tibuok litro parehas sa 1,000 ka mililitro? Katingad-an, 'di ba!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Litmus paper does NOT change color in a neutral solution
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states litmus behavior in a neutral solution. It does not identify solutions found at home/school or classify them as acids, bases, or salts, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Litmus paper does NOT change color in a neutral solution
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single litmus observation for neutral solutions but does not identify common acids, bases, or salts using indicators, nor does it name any specific substances.

copy.en: Litmus paper does NOT change color in a neutral solution, just like in pure water!
copy.tl: Ang litmus paper ay HINDI NAGBABAGO ng kulay sa neutral na solusyon, gaya ng purong tubig!
copy.bis: Ang litmus paper DILI MAUSAB og kolor sa neutral nga solusyon, sama sa lunsay nga tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals that give live birth usually have fewer babies at a time, but they take much better care of them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions live birth but does not identify which groups of animals give birth to live young (e.g., mammals) versus those that lay eggs (e.g., birds, reptiles). It only states a general pattern about offspring number and care, which does not directly support the identification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals that give live birth usually have fewer babies at a time, but they take much better care of them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, nor does it describe any stages from birth/egg/seed to maturity. It is unrelated to the competency's focus on life-cycle comparison.

copy.en: Animals that give live birth usually have fewer babies at a time, but they take much better care of them.
copy.tl: Ang mga hayop na nanganganak ng buhay na anak ay kadalasang kaunti lang ang anak ngunit mas inaalagaan ito.
copy.bis: Ang mga hayop nga nanganak ug buhi nga anak kasagaran pipila lang ka anak apan mas giatiman kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cell has organelles with jobs: the nucleus controls it and holds DNA, mitochondria make energy, cytoplasm is the fluid inside, and the membrane controls what gets in.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the functions of a few cell organelles (nucleus, mitochondria, cytoplasm, membrane) but does not address the competency's core skill of using proper microscope techniques to observe and identify cell parts. It also omits chloroplasts. The content is background knowledge about organelles, not instruction on microscope observation or identification techniques.

copy.en:
What are the tiny parts inside a cell?

A cell has organelles with jobs: the nucleus controls it and holds DNA, mitochondria make energy, cytoplasm is the fluid inside, and the membrane controls what gets in.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mga bahagi ng cell?

Ang cell ay may organelles na may tungkulin: ang nucleus ang kontrol-sentro na may DNA, ang mitochondria ang gumagawa ng enerhiya, ang cytoplasm ang likido sa loob, at ang membrane ang kumokontrol sa pumapasok.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gagmayng bahin sa cell?

Ang cell adunay organelles nga may tahas: ang nucleus mao ang sentro sa kontrol nga may DNA, ang mitochondria maghimo og enerhiya, ang cytoplasm mao ang likido sa sulod, ug ang membrane mokontrol sa mosulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most dinosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago when a huge asteroid struck Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions extinction but does not discuss threats to biodiversity (e.g., habitat loss, pollution, invasive species) or how such threats lead to extinction. It is a specific historical extinction event, not a biodiversity-threat discussion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: today's birds are descendants of small dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that birds are descendants of dinosaurs; it does not present lines of evidence (fossils, biogeography, comparative morphology) supporting evolution. This is a single evolutionary claim, not an explanation of evidence.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most dinosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a date in the past but does not explain how the geologic time scale helps recount Earth's history. It does not address geologic time divisions, dating methods, or the time scale's role.

copy.en:
Why did most dinosaurs disappear?

Most dinosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago when a huge asteroid struck Earth — but today's birds are descendants of small dinosaurs!
copy.tl:
Bakit naglaho ang karamihan sa mga dinosaur?

Karamihan sa mga dinosaur ay naglaho mga 66 milyong taon na ang nakalipas nang tumama ang isang napakalaking asteroid sa Earth — pero ang mga ibon ngayon ay itinuturing na inapo ng maliliit na dinosaur!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga nahanaw ang kadaghanan sa mga dinosaur?

Kadaghanan sa mga dinosaur nahanaw mga 66 ka milyon ka tuig kanhi sa dihang naigo sa Yuta ang usa ka dako kaayong asteroid — apan ang mga langgam karon giisip nga kaliwat sa gagmayng dinosaur!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It means an animal risks disappearing forever from habitat loss and hunting — like the Philippine eagle and tamaraw.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines 'endangered' and gives examples, but does not classify species into critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable using secondary resources. It provides background vocabulary, not the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We help by protecting their homes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to research how to protect and conserve endangered and/or economically important species in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions protecting habitats as a general help, but does not research or describe how to protect and conserve endangered species in the local community. It lacks the research and conservation detail required.

copy.en:
What does 'endangered' mean?

It means an animal risks disappearing forever from habitat loss and hunting — like the Philippine eagle and tamaraw. We help by protecting their homes.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng endangered?

Ibig sabihin, nanganganib nang tuluyang mawala ang isang hayop dahil sa nasirang tirahan at pangangaso — tulad ng Philippine eagle at tamaraw. Tinutulungan natin sila sa pangangalaga ng kanilang habitat.
copy.bis:
Unsay ipasabot sa endangered?

Nagpasabot nga nameligro nga mawala hangtod ang usa ka hayop tungod sa nagub-ang puy-anan ug pagpangayam — sama sa Philippine eagle ug tamaraw. Matabangan nato sila pinaagi sa pag-amping sa ilang habitat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Their chambered shells look exactly like their ancestors from the Paleozoic era over 400 million years ago.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Paleozoic era and deep time, but it does not explain how the geologic time scale helps recount Earth's history. It only uses an era name as background for a living fossil example, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is a 'living fossil' swimming in Philippine seas today?

Living fossils are organisms that have barely changed for millions of years! The nautilus, found in Philippine seas, is one example. Their chambered shells look exactly like their ancestors from the Paleozoic era over 400 million years ago.
copy.tl:
Anong living fossil ang lumalangoy sa dagat ng Pilipinas?

Ang living fossils halos hindi nagbago sa milyun-milyong taon! Ang nautilus sa dagat ng Pilipinas ay isang halimbawa. Ang chambered shells nila ay kapareho pa rin ng ninuno nila sa Paleozoic era mahigit 400 milyong taon na.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang living fossil sa dagat sa Pilipinas?

Ang nautilus! Wala magbag-o sulod sa 400 milyong tuig gikan sa Paleozoic era. Ang chambered shells niini sama ra sa katigulangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A living fossil is an animal or plant alive today that still looks almost the same as its ancestors from ancient times!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines the term 'living fossil.' It does not explain how fossils, biogeography, or comparative morphology serve as lines of evidence for evolution, nor does it use secondary sources to support such an explanation. The concept is tangentially related to fossils but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A living fossil is an animal or plant alive today that still looks almost the same as its ancestors from ancient times!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ancestors and ancient times, which loosely connects to evolution, but it does not address any of the specified concepts (variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation) or involve small-group discussion. It is only a vocabulary definition with no direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
What is a living fossil?

A living fossil is an animal or plant alive today that still looks almost the same as its ancestors from ancient times!
copy.tl:
Ano ang living fossil?

Ang living fossil ay isang buhay na hayop o halaman ngayon na halos kapareho pa rin ng mga ninuno nito mula sa sinaunang panahon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang living fossil?

Ang living fossil usa ka buhi nga hayop o tanom karon nga halos pareho gihapon sa mga katigulangan niini gikan sa karaan kaayo nga panahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: parents pass their traits to their children through genes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions genes and heredity but does not address DNA or chromosomes, nor does it explain their roles in trait transmission. It only gives a general statement that genes pass traits, which is not sufficient to directly support the G9-L-2 competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: parents pass their traits to their children through genes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that genetic information is passed on to offspring from both parents by the process of meiosis and fertilization
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not mention meiosis, fertilization, or the contribution of both parents. It only states that parents pass traits via genes, which is a general heredity concept and not direct support for the specific process of meiosis and fertilization.

copy.en:
Why do children resemble their parents?

In heredity, parents pass their traits to their children through genes — that's why kids inherit things like eye color or leaf shape, so parents and offspring look alike but aren't identical!
copy.tl:
Bakit magkahawig ang mga magulang at anak?

Sa heredity, ipinapasa ng mga magulang ang kanilang mga katangian sa anak sa pamamagitan ng genes — kaya nagmamana ang anak ng mga tulad ng kulay ng mata o hugis ng dahon, kaya magkahawig sila pero hindi magkapareho!
copy.bis:
Nganong managsama ang ginikanan ug anak?

Sa heredity, ipasa sa mga ginikanan ang ilang mga kinaiya ngadto sa anak pinaagi sa genes — mao nga makapanunod ang anak og mga sama sa kolor sa mata o porma sa dahon, busa managsama sila apan dili managsama gyud!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has no hard shell of its own on its tail
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the tail and the lack of a shell, but does not describe outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement or gathering food. The mention of the tail is incidental, not instructional for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: moves to a bigger one as it grows
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation (using a borrowed shell and moving to larger shells as it grows), but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment through mimicry or camouflage. The adaptation is not framed as an evolutionary change, and the competency specifically targets examples like mimicry or camouflage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: moves to a bigger one as it grows
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth ('as it grows') but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Growth is only a passing reference, not an explanation of the characteristic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It lives inside an empty shell from a dead snail
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a hermit crab using a dead snail's shell, which is a form of dependence on another living thing, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs. The shell use is not presented as meeting a basic need (shelter) in the context of interdependence.

copy.en:
Why does a hermit crab borrow a shell?

Because it has no hard shell of its own on its tail! It lives inside an empty shell from a dead snail, and moves to a bigger one as it grows.
copy.tl:
Bakit humihiram ng kabibe ang hermit crab?

Dahil wala itong sariling matigas na kabibe sa buntot! Naninirahan ito sa walang laman na kabibe ng patay na kuhol, at lumilipat sa mas malaki habang lumalaki ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong nanghulam og kabhang ang hermit crab?

Kay wala kini kaugalingong gahi nga kabhang sa ikog! Mopuyo kini sulod sa walay sulod nga kabhang sa patay nga kuhol, ug mobalhin sa mas dako samtang motubo kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bioluminescence is when a living organism uses chemicals in its body to emit light, like a firefly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes bioluminescence, a chemical light-emitting process in living organisms, which is unrelated to the competency about describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. No instructional support for mixtures.

copy.en: Bioluminescence is when a living organism uses chemicals in its body to emit light, like a firefly.
copy.tl: Ang bioluminescence ay kapag ang isang buhay na organismo ay gumagamit ng mga kemikal sa katawan nito upang maglabas ng liwanag, tulad ng alitaptap.
copy.bis: Ang bioluminescence mao ang dihang ang usa ka buhing organismo mogamit og mga kemikal sa iyang lawas aron magpagawas og kahayag, sama sa aninipot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pinggang Pinoy divides food into three groups
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the Pinggang Pinoy food group classification (GO, GROW, GLOW) and nutrient roles, not the identification of basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). Food is one basic need, but the card does not address the concept of basic needs or the other needs; it is only topically related through food.

copy.en: Pinggang Pinoy divides food into three groups: GO (energy, like rice), GROW (protein, like fish and eggs), and GLOW (vitamins, like fruits and veggies).
copy.tl: Hinahati ng Pinggang Pinoy ang pagkain sa tatlo: GO (enerhiya, tulad ng kanin), GROW (protina, tulad ng isda at itlog), at GLOW (bitamina, tulad ng gulay at prutas).
copy.bis: Gibahin sa Pinggang Pinoy ang pagkaon sa tulo: GO (enerhiya, sama sa kan-on), GROW (protina, sama sa isda ug itlog), ug GLOW (bitamina, sama sa utanon ug prutas).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Living organisms can change abiotic factors
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how living organisms alter abiotic factors (e.g., tree roots breaking rocks into soil). This is a life-science/ecology concept, not about sources of light, light behavior, or uses of light. It does not support the G3-F-6 competency in any way.

copy.en: Living organisms can change abiotic factors through their activities, like tree roots breaking rocks into smaller pieces of soil.
copy.tl: Maaaring baguhin ng mga buhay na organismo ang abiotic factors sa pamamagitan ng kanilang mga gawain, tulad ng mga ugat ng puno na nagbabasag sa mga bato upang maging maliliit na piraso ng lupa.
copy.bis: Ang mga buhi nga organismo makausab sa abiotic factors pinaagi sa ilang mga kalihokan, sama sa mga gamot sa kahoy nga nagabuak sa mga bato aron mahimong gagmay nga piraso sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the cells in our body multiply and get bigger!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that growth occurs because cells multiply and get bigger, which is a basic prerequisite idea for cellular reproduction. However, it does not mention the two types of cell division (mitosis and meiosis) nor describe mitosis as division for growth and repair, so it does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
Why do our bodies grow bigger?

Because the cells in our body multiply and get bigger! Food gives us the 'building blocks,' especially protein, to make new cells.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo lumalaki?

Dahil dumarami at lumalaki ang mga cell sa ating katawan! Nagbibigay ang pagkain ng 'building blocks,' lalo na ang protina, para makagawa ng bagong cell.
copy.bis:
Nganong motubo kita?

Kay modaghan ug modako ang mga cell sa atong lawas! Ang pagkaon naghatag sa 'building blocks,' ilabi na ang protina, aron makahimo og bag-ong cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's loam! It is a perfect mix of sand, clay, and humus for your plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that loam is best for growing plants and describes its composition, but it does not support the competency's focus on participating in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on plant growth. No investigation, comparison of soil types, or effect on growth is presented.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's loam! It is a perfect mix of sand, clay, and humus for your plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions loam as a mix of sand, clay, and humus, but it does not involve guided activities using simple equipment to compare different soil types or compare water-holding ability. It only names loam's components without any comparison or equipment-based activity.

copy.en:
What is the best soil for growing plants?

It's loam! It is a perfect mix of sand, clay, and humus for your plants.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamainam na soil para sa pagtatanim?

Ito ay ang loam! Ito ay timpla ng sand, clay, at humus para sa mga halaman.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang labing maayo nga soil para sa pagtanom?

Kini mao ang loam! Kini sagol sa sand, clay, ug humus para sa mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lodestone is a naturally magnetic rock that attracts iron
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single property of a magnet (attracts iron) but does not support the competency's core action of carrying out guided investigations to identify properties of magnets, including effects on other magnets and objects of different materials. It is background knowledge about a natural magnet, not instruction for the investigation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lodestone is a naturally magnetic rock that attracts iron
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of how objects can affect other objects even when they are not in contact with each other, such as magnets attracting other objects, light from the sun, and loud noises hurting our ears
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a magnet attracting iron, which is one example of non-contact action, but it does not teach the broader concept of objects affecting other objects without contact (e.g., comparing with light or sound). It is a single illustrative fact, not direct support for identifying examples of non-contact effects.

copy.en:
What is a lodestone?

Lodestone is a naturally magnetic rock that attracts iron even though no person made it! It was the first magnet ever known.
copy.tl:
Ano ang lodestone?

Ang lodestone ay isang likas na magnet na bato na umaakit ng bakal kahit hindi ginawa ng tao! Ito ang unang nakilalang magnet.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang lodestone?

Ang lodestone usa ka natural nga magnetikong bato nga modani ug puthaw bisan walay tawo nga naghimo niini! Mao kini ang unang nailhan nga magnet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lolong measured 6.17 meters long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card only reports a length in meters. It does not describe the science process skill of measuring or any other process skill, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How long was Lolong the crocodile?

Lolong measured 6.17 meters long — a certified world record.
copy.tl:
Gaano kahaba si Lolong na buwaya?

Si Lolong ay 6.17 metro ang haba, na ginawang opisyal na rekord ng mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas si Lolong nga buaya?

Si Lolong 6.17 ka metro ang gitas-on, nga gihimong opisyal nga rekord sa kalibotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climate change is a long-term warming or cooling of Earth's climate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines climate change and its effects; it contains no content about reflection or refraction of light, mirrors, lenses, or prisms. The competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Climate change is a long-term warming or cooling of Earth's climate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes climate change and its effects but does not mention renewable energies, societal use of renewables, or mitigation strategies. It shares the broad topic of climate change but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's action of explaining how increased renewable energy use could mitigate climate change.

copy.en: Climate change is a long-term warming or cooling of Earth's climate, with effects including rising sea levels, droughts, water shortages, crop failure, floods, and extreme weather.
copy.tl: Ang climate change ay pangmatagalang pag-init o paglamig ng klima ng Earth, na may mga epektong tulad ng pagtaas ng sea level, tagtuyot, kakulangan sa tubig, pagkasira ng pananim, baha, at matinding panahon.
copy.bis: Ang climate change mao ang dugay nga pag-init o pagbugnaw sa klima sa Yuta, nga may mga epekto sama sa pagsaka sa sea level, hulaw, kakulang sa tubig, pagkadaot sa tanom, baha, ug grabeng panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A long, thin wire has more resistance than a short, thick wire made of the same metal.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about how wire length and thickness affect resistance, but the competency requires guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery. The card does not address current, voltage, circuits, or the investigative process; it only provides a related fact about resistance.

copy.en:
Does wire shape change its resistance?

Yes! A long, thin wire has more resistance than a short, thick wire made of the same metal.
copy.tl:
Nakakaapekto ba ang hugis ng wire sa resistance?

Oo! Ang mahaba at manipis na wire ay may mas mataas na resistance kaysa sa maikli at makapal na wire na gawa sa parehong metal.
copy.bis:
Makaapekto ba ang porma sa wire sa resistance?

Oo! Ang taas ug nipis nga wire mas dako ug resistance kaysa mubo ug baga nga wire nga hinimo sa samang metal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Arctic tern wins! It flies about 70,000 kilometers every year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a migratory behavior, not an evolutionary change or adaptation (such as mimicry or camouflage) that better suits an animal to its environment. Migration is a behavioral pattern, not a structural or physiological change, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It flies about 70,000 kilometers every year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a distance traveled but does not involve measuring distance or time using simple equipment, nor does it describe any measurement process. It only states a known distance, so it does not directly support the competency of accurate measurement.

copy.en:
Which animal migrates the farthest each year?

The Arctic tern wins! It flies about 70,000 kilometers every year, traveling all the way between the Arctic and Antarctic.
copy.tl:
Aling hayop ang may pinakamahabang paglipat bawat taon?

Ang Arctic tern! Lumilipad ito ng mga 70,000 kilometro bawat taon, mula Arctic hanggang Antarctic.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mananap ang adunay pinakataas nga paglalin matag tuig?

Ang Arctic tern! Molupad kini og mga 70,000 ka kilometro matag tuig, gikan sa Arctic hangtod sa Antarctic.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the location and distribution of active volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and major mountain belts to the distribution of oceanic crust and continental crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the Mid-Ocean Ridge as an underwater mountain range, but it does not relate its location or distribution to oceanic versus continental crust, nor does it mention volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, or mountain belts in that framework.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the Mid-Ocean Ridge, stretching over 65,000 kilometers under the sea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the locations of major mountains, faults, volcanos, and ocean trenches using a map of the Philippine Archipelago, and interpret the features in relation to plate tectonics
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a major mountain range but does not locate it on a map of the Philippine Archipelago, nor does it interpret the feature in relation to plate tectonics.

copy.en: Did you know the longest mountain range on Earth is underwater? It is the Mid-Ocean Ridge, stretching over 65,000 kilometers under the sea!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na ang pinakamahabang hanay ng bundok sa mundo ay nasa ilalim ng tubig? Ito ang Mid-Ocean Ridge, umaabot ng mahigit 65,000 kilometro!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang kinahabang han-ay sa bukid sa kalibotan anaa sa ilalom sa tubig? Kini ang Mid-Ocean Ridge, miabot ug kapin sa 65,000 ka kilometro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A longitudinal wave needs the medium to squeeze and spring back along the travel line!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of longitudinal waves only. It does not mention transverse waves or compare the two, so it does not directly support the competency of identifying differences and similarities between longitudinal and transverse waves. It is related background knowledge but not the comparison itself.

copy.en:
What does a longitudinal wave need?

A longitudinal wave needs the medium to squeeze and spring back along the travel line! Luckily, air, water, and solids can all do this.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kailangan ng longitudinal wave?

Ang longitudinal wave ay kailangang pisilin at bumalik sa haba ng travel line! At swerte, kaya itong gawin ng hangin, tubig, at mga solid.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kinahanglan sa longitudinal wave?

Ang longitudinal wave kinahanglan nga mapislon ug mobalik sa travel line! Ug swerte, kaya kini buhaton sa hangin, tubig, ug mga solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A loose, dirty, or corroded connection interrupts the current flow through the metal contacts!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses current flow interruption but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons nor address safe handling of electricity, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A loose, dirty, or corroded connection interrupts the current flow through the metal contacts!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns connection quality in a circuit, not designing/constructing a circuit to identify conductors and insulators or testing materials from the environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even if the circuit looks complete, that broken path means the bulb won't light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a bulb fails due to a broken path, but it does not teach assembling or drawing a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer.

copy.en:
Why won't the bulb light up even if the circuit looks complete?

A loose, dirty, or corroded connection interrupts the current flow through the metal contacts! Even if the circuit looks complete, that broken path means the bulb won't light.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi sumisindag ang bombilya kahit mukhang kumpleto ang circuit?

Ang maluwag, marumi, o kinakalawang na koneksyon ay naaabala ang daloy ng kuryente sa metal! Kahit mukhang kumpleto ang circuit, mapuputol ang daanan kaya hindi mag-iilaw ang bombilya.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili modan-ag ang bombilya bisan mukhang kompleto ang sirkito?

Ang luag, hugaw, o gikalawang nga koneksyon maputol ang dagan sa kuryente sa metal! Bisan kompleto ang sirkito, maputol ang agianan mao nga dili modan-ag ang bombilya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Energy is lost at each trophic level
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains energy loss in food chains/trophic levels, which is an ecology topic. G8-E-7 is about typhoon development and why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. No connection to typhoons or Earth/space content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Energy is lost at each trophic level
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy transfer in ecosystems, not how solar energy interacts with the atmosphere. G7-E-9 is about the Sun's energy and atmospheric interactions, which is unrelated to trophic-level energy loss.

copy.en: Energy is lost at each trophic level because organisms use much of it for their own functions and some is lost as heat.
copy.tl: Nawawalan ng energy sa bawat trophic level dahil ginagamit ng mga organismo ang malaking bahagi nito para sa sarili nilang mga gawain at ang iba ay nawawala bilang init.
copy.bis: Mawad-an ug energy sa matag trophic level tungod kay gigamit sa mga organismo ang dakong bahin niini alang sa ilang kaugalingong mga gimbuhaton ug ang uban mawala isip init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: then sprout once there is enough water and warmth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and warmth as conditions for sprouting, but it does not identify the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as a general concept. It is an example of a seed needing water, not a lesson on basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: then sprout once there is enough water and warmth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a seed sprouting (growth) after a long dormancy, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It is a specific fact about seed longevity, not instruction on the characteristics.

copy.en:
How long can a lotus seed stay alive?

A lotus seed is so tough it can stay alive in the mud for hundreds of years, then sprout once there is enough water and warmth.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabubuhay ang buto ng lotus?

Napakatibay ng buto ng lotus kaya nakakapanatiling buhay sa putik nang daan-daang taon, bago tumubo kapag may sapat na tubig at init.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang binhi sa lotus?

Lig-on kaayo ang binhi sa lotus nga makapabilin nga buhi sa lapok sulod sa gatosan ka tuig, una moturok kon adunay igong tubig ug kainit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air gets thinner with less oxygen in each breath, making people get out of breath and tired more easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathing and tiredness but does not describe how the respiratory system (or any body system) works. It only notes that less oxygen per breath causes breathlessness, which is a fact about air composition, not an explanation of respiratory system function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air gets thinner with less oxygen in each breath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen in air but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only states that air has less oxygen at high altitude, which is not the competency's focus on air composition.

copy.en:
Why do you get tired easily on high mountains?

As you climb high, the air gets thinner with less oxygen in each breath, making people get out of breath and tired more easily!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling mapagod sa mataas na bundok?

Habang umaakyat ka, mas manipis ang hangin at mas kaunti ang oxygen sa bawat hininga, kaya mas madaling mahingal at mapagod ang mga tao!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas dali makapoy sa taas nga bukid?

Samtang mosaka ka, mas nipis ang hangin ug mas gamay ang oxygen sa matag ginhawa, mao nga mas dali maghangos ug makapoy ang mga tawo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When water gets trapped in a low place with no way to drain out, it just collects there and gets deeper and deeper!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water pooling in low areas, which could be a consequence of heavy rain from a weather disturbance, but it does not mention any weather disturbance, its effects, or the Philippines. It only states a general topographic fact about water accumulation, providing no direct instructional support for describing effects of weather disturbances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When water gets trapped in a low place with no way to drain out, it just collects there and gets deeper and deeper!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water collecting in low places but does not involve comparing soil types, using simple equipment, or testing water-holding ability of sandy, clay, silt, or loam soils. It is only tangentially related to water and soil drainage, not to the specific guided activity of comparing soil types.

copy.en: When water gets trapped in a low place with no way to drain out, it just collects there and gets deeper and deeper!
copy.tl: Kapag naipon ang tubig sa mababang lugar at walang labasan, naiipon lang ito doon at lalong lumalalim!
copy.bis: Kon ang tubig sa ubos nga dapit walay agianan pagawas, magtipon lang kini didto ug magkalawom og kalawom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a place with low air pressure where air rises to form clouds and rain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure, clouds, and rain, which are weather characteristics, but it does not teach students to identify the basic characteristics used to describe weather. It explains a low pressure area as a weather system, not the set of weather descriptors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sometimes growing into a typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that an LPA can sometimes grow into a typhoon. It does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is a Low Pressure Area (LPA)?

It's a place with low air pressure where air rises to form clouds and rain, sometimes growing into a typhoon!
copy.tl:
Ano ang Low Pressure Area (LPA)?

Ito ay lugar na mababa ang presyon ng hangin, kaya umaakyat ito para bumuo ng ulap at ulan, na minsan nagiging bagyo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang Low Pressure Area (LPA)?

Mao kini ang lugar nga ubos ang presyon sa hangin, busa mosaka aron mohimo og panganod ug ulan, ug usahay motubo sa bagyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Microbes need water to multiply, so in dry food they can hardly grow at all!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses microbial growth in dry food, not the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions. Although food preservation is mentioned in the competency, the card does not address chemical reaction rates, so it only shares the broad food-preservation context.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Microbes need water to multiply, so in dry food they can hardly grow at all!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about microbial growth and moisture, not chemical properties of materials such as burning, reacting, or biodegradability. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Microbes need water to multiply, so in dry food they can hardly grow at all!
copy.tl: Ang mga mikrobyo ay nangangailangan ng tubig upang dumami, kaya sa tuyong pagkain ay halos hindi sila makalago!
copy.bis: Ang mga mikrobyo nagkinahanglan og tubig aron modaghan, mao nga sa uga nga pagkaon halos dili sila makatubo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has a frequency of 27.5 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions frequency, a wave property term, but does not describe how wave properties are described using scientific terms, nor does it involve research from secondary sources. It is a trivia fact about a piano note, not instruction on wave properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has a frequency of 27.5 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a specific musical note's frequency, not about how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations. It does not explore sound production or transfer, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What is the lowest note on a piano?

The lowest note is A0, and it has a frequency of 27.5 Hz!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamababang nota sa piano?

Ang pinakamababang nota ay A0, at mayroon itong dalas na 27.5 Hz!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakaubos nga nota sa piano?

Ang pinakaubos nga nota mao ang A0, ug adunay frequency nga 27.5 Hz!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: comes from the lightest parts of crude oil that collect as gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that LPG comes from the lightest parts of crude oil, but it does not mention any mixture separation technique (e.g., fractional distillation) or explain its benefits. It only identifies a product origin, not a separation process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: LPG cooking gas used in many Filipino kitchens comes from the lightest parts of crude oil that collect as gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gas and crude oil (liquid), but it does not teach the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or their identification. It only uses the word 'gas' in a product context, not as a state-of-matter concept.

copy.en:
Where does our LPG cooking gas come from?

The LPG cooking gas used in many Filipino kitchens comes from the lightest parts of crude oil that collect as gas!
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang ating LPG cooking gas?

Ang LPG cooking gas na ginagamit sa maraming kusinang Pilipino ay galing sa pinakamagagaang bahagi ng crude oil na naipon bilang gas!
copy.bis:
Gikan asa ang atong LPG cooking gas?

Ang LPG cooking gas nga gigamit sa daghang kusinang Pilipino gikan sa pinakagaan nga mga bahin sa crude oil nga matipon isip gas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The rice grains soak up water, swell, and make the mixture thick and soft.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents lugaw as an everyday mixture but does not describe it as uniform or non-uniform, nor compare it to solutions or suspensions. It focuses on starch swelling, not mixture classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The rice grains soak up water, swell, and make the mixture thick and soft.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a change in texture (thick and soft) but does not describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The swelling of rice grains is not a direct example of the target solid-material properties.

copy.en: Lugaw is rice boiled in plenty of water! The rice grains soak up water, swell, and make the mixture thick and soft.
copy.tl: Ang lugaw ay bigas na pinakuluan sa maraming tubig! Ang butil ng bigas ay sumisipsip ng tubig, namamaga, at lumalapot ang halo.
copy.bis: Ang lugaw mao ang bugas nga gilutoan sa daghang tubig! Ang lugas sa bugas mosuyop ug tubig, moburot, ug mohimo sa sagol nga baga ug humok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you must jump at just the right moment as the rope spins around
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about timing a jump relative to the rope's motion, but it does not introduce or support the concept of speed (distance moved in a given time). No distance, time, or speed relationship is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you must jump at just the right moment as the rope spins around
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves movement and timing but does not measure or describe changes in position relative to an original position (closer, farther, left, right). It does not support the measurement or description skill of this competency.

copy.en: In jump rope (luksong-lubid), you must jump at just the right moment as the rope spins around so it passes safely under your feet!
copy.tl: Sa luksong-lubid, kailangan mong lumukso sa tamang sandali habang umiikot ang lubid upang dumaan ito nang maayos sa ilalim ng iyong paa!
copy.bis: Sa luksong-lubid, kinahanglan molukso ka sa husto nga higayon samtang nagtuyok ang pisi aron molabay kini sa ubos sa imong tiil!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A lunar eclipse is totally safe to watch with your bare eyes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses safety of watching a lunar eclipse, contrasting the Moon's gentle light with the Sun's. It does not describe any safety measures to avoid harmful effects of the Sun's light, which is the focus of G3-E-9. The topic is related to celestial objects and safety but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A lunar eclipse is totally safe to watch with your bare eyes! The Moon's light is very gentle and soft, unlike the Sun's.
copy.tl: Ligtas tingnan ang lunar eclipse gamit ang ating mga mata! Mahina at malambing lang ang liwanag ng Buwan, hindi tulad ng Araw.
copy.bis: Luwas tan-awon ang lunar eclipse gamit ang atong mga mata! Huyang lang ang kahayag sa Bulan, dili sama sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Regular exercise like running or basketball strengthens your lungs and breathing muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and breathing muscles but does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It focuses on the effect of exercise, not on anatomy or function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Regular exercise like running or basketball strengthens your lungs and breathing muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the respiratory system indirectly by mentioning lungs and breathing muscles, but it does not describe how the respiratory system works. It is about exercise benefits, not system function.

copy.en:
Why don't athletes get out of breath?

Regular exercise like running or basketball strengthens your lungs and breathing muscles — that's why athletes can keep going longer without gasping for air!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi kaagad nahihingal ang mga atleta?

Ang regular na ehersisyo gaya ng pagtakbo o basketball ay nagpapalakas ng baga at kalamnan sa paghinga — kaya matagal na tumatakbo ang mga atleta nang hindi agad naghihingal!
copy.bis:
Ngano dili dali maghangos ang mga atleta?

Ang regular nga ehersisyo sama sa pagdagan o basketball nagpalig-on sa baga ug sa unod sa paghinga — mao nga makahawid og dugay ang mga atleta nga dili dali maghangos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your voice is made by air leaving your lungs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs and air leaving them, but it does not identify the respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how the respiratory system works. It focuses on voice production via the voice box and vocal cords, which is not the competency's target.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your voice is made by air leaving your lungs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs but does not describe how the respiratory system works in simple terms. It explains voice production, not the functioning of the respiratory system as a body system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: vibrates two thin flaps called vocal cords
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that air vibrates vocal cords to make voice, which relates to how sound is made, but it does not explore or describe sound transfer in everyday situations such as a ringing bell or hearing noises. It is a specific biological explanation rather than a general sound lesson.

copy.en:
What really makes your voice?

Your voice is made by air leaving your lungs! It passes through your voice box and vibrates two thin flaps called vocal cords — that's why you can't talk without breathing out.
copy.tl:
Ano talaga ang gumagawa ng iyong boses?

Ang boses mo ay gawa ng hanging lumalabas sa iyong baga! Dumadaan ito sa voice box at niyayanig nito ang dalawang manipis na vocal cords — kaya hindi ka makapagsalita nang hindi humihinga.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang naghimo sa imong tingog?

Ang imong tingog gihimo sa hangin nga mogawas sa baga! Moagi kini sa voice box ug mopakurog sa duha ka nipis nga vocal cords — mao nga dili ka makasulti kon dili ka mogawas og gininhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Baguio City was hit the worst by the 1990 Luzon earthquake, and several buildings collapsed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific earthquake's impact on a city but does not describe how effects depend on magnitude, nor does it compare effects across different magnitudes. copy.en: Baguio City was hit the worst by the 1990 Luzon earthquake, and several buildings collapsed!
copy.tl: Ang Lungsod ng Baguio ang pinakatinamaan ng lindol sa Luzon noong 1990, at gumuho ang ilang gusali!
copy.bis: Ang Dakbayan sa Baguio mao ang pinakagrabe nga naigo sa linog sa Luzon niadtong 1990, ug nangaguba ang pipila ka building!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: magnitude of 7.7
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the magnitude of a specific earthquake and that it was one of the strongest. It does not describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on magnitude, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: The 1990 Luzon earthquake had a massive magnitude of 7.7, making it one of the strongest earthquakes in the Philippines!
copy.tl: Ang lindol sa Luzon noong 1990 ay may lakas na magnitude 7.7, na ginagawa itong isa sa pinakamalakas sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Ang linog sa Luzon niadtong 1990 adunay kusog nga magnitude 7.7, nga naghimo niini nga usa sa pinakakusog sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: studies it under a microscope
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions using a microscope but does not teach the parts, functions, or proper handling/storing of a compound microscope. It describes a medical biopsy procedure, not microscope equipment or its use.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: studies it under a microscope
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions examining a lymph node under a microscope but does not teach techniques for observing or identifying cell parts such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, or chloroplasts. It is about a diagnostic biopsy, not cell observation skills.

copy.en: Sometimes a doctor takes a tiny piece of a lymph node and studies it under a microscope to find out what disease the body is fighting.
copy.tl: Minsan kumukuha ang doktor ng maliit na piraso ng kulani at tinitingnan ito sa mikroskopyo para malaman kung anong sakit ang nilalabanan ng katawan.
copy.bis: Usahay mokuha ang doktor og gamay nga piraso sa kulani ug tan-awon kini sa mikroskopyo aron mahibaloan kung unsang sakit ang gisumpo sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother monkey carries and cares for her baby until it's all grown up.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the baby grows up, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is a narrative about maternal care, not instruction on living-thing characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother monkey carries and cares for her baby until it's all grown up.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to a mammal's growth from baby to adult, but it does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants, nor does it present stages from birth to adulthood in a comparative way.

copy.en: A mother monkey carries and cares for her baby until it's all grown up.
copy.tl: Kinakalong at inaalagaan ng inang unggoy ang anak nito hanggang lumaki ito.
copy.bis: Ang inahan nga unggoy nagkugos ug nag-atiman sa iyang anak hangtod modako kini.

Can you turn an iron nail into a magnet?

Yes! If you rub an iron nail with a magnet, it can become a temporary magnet!
copy.tl:
Kaya mo bang gawing magneto ang isang pako?

Oo! Kapag ikinuskos mo ang isang pako sa magneto, ito ay maaaring maging pansamantalang magneto!
copy.bis:
Mahimo ba nimo nga magneto ang usa ka lansang?

Oo! Kung imong haplosan ang usa ka lansang sa magneto, ang lansang mahimong temporaryo nga magneto!

copy.en: Neodymium magnets are the strongest permanent magnets! With a powerful magnetic field in a small size, they are used in hard drives, earphones, EV motors, and wind turbines.
copy.tl: Ang neodymium magnets ang pinakamalakas na permanent magnets! Dahil sa malakas na magnetic field sa maliit na sukat, ginagamit sila sa hard drives, earphones, EV motors, at wind turbines.
copy.bis: Ang neodymium magnets mao ang pinakamalakas nga permanent magnets! Tungod sa kusog nga magnetic field sa gamay nga sukat, gigamit kini sa hard drives, earphones, EV motors, ug wind turbines.

copy.en:
Why does a magnet barely stick to very thin iron?

When iron is super thin, there aren't enough magnetic domains for a strong pull. The magnet might barely stick or not at all—you need enough iron for it to really grip!
copy.tl:
Bakit halos hindi dumidikit ang magnet sa napakamanipis na bakal?

Kapag manipis na manipis ang iron, kulang ang magnetic domains para sa malakas na hila. Baka halos hindi dumikit o sadyang hindi na—kailangan ng sapat na iron para talagang kumapit!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga halos dili modikit ang magnet sa nipis kaayo nga puthaw?

Kon nipis kaayo ang iron, kulang ang magnetic domains para sa kusog nga bira. Basin halos dili modikit o dili na gyud—kinahanglan og igo nga iron para tinuod nga makakapit!

What is the difference between a permanent magnet and an electromagnet?

A permanent magnet is always magnetic and used in earphones! An electromagnet can be switched on and off, making it perfect for scrapyard cranes and doorbells.

Ano ang pagkakaiba ng permanent magnet at electromagnet?

Ang permanent magnet ay laging may magnetismo at ginagamit sa mga earphone! Ang electromagnet naman ay pwedeng i-on at i-off, kaya ginagamit ito sa mga doorbell at crane.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa permanent magnet ug electromagnet?

Ang permanent magnet kanunay adunay magnetismo ug gigamit sa mga earphone! Ang electromagnet mahimong i-on ug i-off, busa gigamit kini sa mga doorbell ug crane.

copy.bis: Ani ang usa ka nindot nga lagda sa magnet: walay magnet nga mahimong adunay usa ra ka polo — kanunay adunay N ug S nga polo ang matag magnet!

What makes an electromagnet different from a regular magnet?

An electromagnet gets its strength from electricity! Switch the current on, and the pole gets strong. Switch it off, and the pull disappears. A regular magnet is always strong.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng electromagnet sa karaniwang magnet?

Ang lakas ng electromagnet ay galing sa kuryente! Buksan mo ang kuryente, lalakas ang pole. Patayin mo, mawawala ang hila. Ang karaniwang magnet ay laging may lakas.

Unsay kalainan sa electromagnet sa ordinaryong magnet?

Ang kusog sa electromagnet gikan sa kuryente! Ablihi ang kuryente, mokusog ang pole. Palonga, mawala ang pagbira. Ang ordinaryong magnet kanunay adunay kusog.
